title: A global movement linking cultural heritage and climate resilience gathers momentum at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye
content:
As COP31 drew to a close in Antalya, Türkiye, on 22 November 2026 with a record-breaking 50-hour extension, governments ultimately concluded the summit without reaching an overarching agreement on key issues, despite increasing pressure on vulnerable communities and the prospect of further extreme climate events. Yet, alongside the negotiations, another important story unfolded: the growing recognition of culture and cultural heritage as essential resources for climate action, adaptation and resilience. Through two weeks of international dialogue, partnerships, and practical initiatives, Europa Nostra, the European Heritage Hub and its partners demonstrated how cultural heritage can contribute to a more resilient and sustainable future.

title: Europa Nostra participates in the EU Culture Dialogue first annual meeting hosted by Commissioner Micallef in Brussels
content:
On 12 November 2026, Europa Nostra participated in the first annual meeting of the EU Culture Dialogue held in Brussels. Led by Glenn Micallef, European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, the event marked the first anniversary of the adoption of the Culture Compass for Europe. Europa Nostra’s Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović took part in the meeting, alongside 60 representatives of cultural organisations and creative sectors from across Europe.
